chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated on the authority of Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He who withholds a Qirat of the zakat is neither a believer nor a Muslim.
And this is His saying, Exalted and Mighty: 'My Lord, send me back, that I might do righteousness in that which I have left.'
And in another narration: And his prayer is not accepted.

key_terms.رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ: My Lord, send me back (Quranic quote)
key_terms.قِيرَاطاً: A small unit of weight or coin, used here to denote even a minimal amount of zakat

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of withholding zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith emphasizes the severity of neglecting zakat by linking it to the Quranic verse (23:99) where the deceased plead for return to perform good deeds, implying that withholding zakat constitutes a failure to fulfill a fundamental pillar of faith. The narration further clarifies that this omission not only affects one's status as a believer but also invalidates the acceptance of their prayers, highlighting the interconnectedness of obligatory acts in Shia jurisprudence.
